claims.text: Premelting in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is primarily governed by local lattice distortions caused by atomic-size differences and chemical disparity.
Local lattice distortions create heterogeneous energy landscapes.
These heterogeneous energy landscapes locally lower the activation energy for atomic diffusion at surfaces and grain boundaries.
Enhanced diffusion at distorted surfaces and grain boundaries causes premelting to begin below the bulk melting point.
The initial nanoparticles are homogeneously mixed and single phase.
The initial nanoparticles have a uniform elemental distribution.
Atomic-size mismatch produces significant local lattice strain in the initial nanoparticles.
Rapid quenching preserves high atomic disorder and atomic mixing.
Annealing promotes partial phase segregation.
Annealing-induced partial phase segregation reduces local lattice distortion.
Localized lattice strain creates regions of lower energetic stability that are more susceptible to atomic mobility.
Highly strained regions act as nucleation sites for premelting as temperature increases.
Regions with greater distortion develop surface liquid-like behavior earlier than regions with less distortion.
More highly disordered nanoparticles will exhibit premelting at lower temperatures than annealed, partially segregated nanoparticles.
Premelting will be observable as increased surface diffusion or partial loss of crystallinity at nanoparticle edges.
Annealed, partially segregated nanoparticles will have higher apparent premelting-onset temperatures than rapidly quenched nanoparticles.
Surface and grain-boundary effects dominate premelting behavior for nanoparticles approximately 5–50 nm in size.
The comparison should use identical nominal compositions and differ only in processing history intended to alter atomic mixing and lattice strain.
Premelting onset can be assessed by in-situ TEM or calorimetry while local lattice strain is characterized by electron or X-ray diffraction.
Statistically indistinguishable premelting-onset temperatures and surface behavior in the quenched and annealed samples would falsify local lattice distortion as the governing factor.
